subject: Implementation plan: No-model-learning contractual guardrails & transfer map
messages:
From: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@healthworks.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@healthworks.com, HealthWorks Legal <legal@healthworks.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data use and model improvement (HealthWorks POC)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement/Legal here have a few follow-ups before we proceed to pilot. High-level asks: 

1) We need a contractual commitment that HealthWorks data will not be used to improve or retrain any models (no-model-learning / no-train).
2) A current list of subprocessors and the physical locations where customer data might be processed or at-rest backups may be stored.
3) The technical path for exports (SFTP vs API), and whether we can get an escrow copy of logs/outputs if required for audit.

Can you confirm those items and share any evidence pack or proposed contract language? We have a target sign-off window of 2 weeks.

Appreciate it —
Aaron
Aaron Cole
Head of Procurement, HealthWorks Inc.
aaron.cole@healthworks.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@healthworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, HealthWorks Legal <legal@healthworks.com>, procurement@healthworks.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data use and model improvement (HealthWorks POC)

Aaron —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise implementation plan and what we'll provide this week.

Summary of commitments (proposed addendum):
- No-model-learning: Redwood will not use HealthWorks production data to improve, train, or tune any model variants serving your traffic. This includes aggregate training, fine-tuning, or offline model retraining.
- Prompt/response ownership: HealthWorks retains rights to prompts and generated outputs (tenant outputs). Redwood will not assert derivative ownership over those outputs.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide an up-to-date subprocessor inventory and prior notice of relevant changes.
- Cross-border transfers: We will document which subprocessors process data in which jurisdictions and provide residency options where available.

Deliverables this week (target Fri 2027-07-09):
1) Proposed DPA addendum redline (attached) — legal-friendly no-train language and operational obligations.
2) Subprocessor inventory snapshot (attached CSV) with host country, role, and contact.
3) Export/escrow specification doc (attached) describing SFTP export cadence, retention, and hashing for verification.

Operational notes (cc: Marissa / Dev):
- We can enable an operational toggle to segregate HealthWorks traffic to a non-logging route and short-lived KV caches for the pilot. This reduces the telemetry surface for model-improvement pipelines.
- SFTP export: nightly bundle of tenant outputs + audit logs. We support encrypted SFTP push; retention & delivery SLA to be agreed.

Next steps: please review the redline and let us know any specific language HealthWorks Legal wants adjusted. If procurement prefers a DocuSign flow, send the envelope details and we'll ingest.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Privacy & Trust (Redwood Inference)
hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com

(attachments: redline_dpa_no_train_addendum.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_snapshot.csv, sftp-escrow-spec.docx)

From: legal@healthworks.com
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@healthworks.com>, procurement@healthworks.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Data use and model improvement (HealthWorks POC)

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed the redline and have two items that need clarification before we proceed: 

1) Scope of "no-model-learning": please confirm whether this applies to all environments (prod, staging, logs, support tickets) and whether aggregated / de-identified datasets are also excluded. We need explicit language covering ephemeral logs and support traces.

2) Subprocessor residency: your inventory lists a shared compute provider in a third country (Country X). We require evidence that no tenant data will be used in any model-improvement pipeline in that region, and whether it will be replicated outside the US for backups.

Additionally, our security team asked for a one-page operational summary describing where outputs and audit logs are stored, how long they are retained, and the process for producing an escrow export if legal/regulatory audit is triggered.

Could Marissa or Dev provide the ops summary and confirm the point about backups/replication?

Thanks —
HealthWorks Legal
legal@healthworks.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: legal@healthworks.com, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@healthworks.com>, procurement@healthworks.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data use and model improvement (HealthWorks POC)

Hi Legal / Hannah —

Quick ops summary attached (condensed below as requested):

- Environments in scope: The no-train commitment applies to production and staging endpoints that process HealthWorks tenant IDs; ephemeral developer sandboxes are excluded if explicitly flagged (we will not route production tenant IDs to developer sandboxes).
- Logs & support traces: Access logs and structured audit logs are retained for 30 days by default for troubleshooting; these are excluded from training pipelines by design. Longer retention can be configured per contract.
- Subprocessor in Country X: compute nodes in Country X are used for short-lived inference capacity during bursts; persistent storage/backups for HealthWorks tenant data are NOT stored in Country X. Backup replicas are in the US-only region for this agreement; we will annotate the inventory CSV to show that.
- Escrow/export: We support encrypted SFTP push of nightly bundles (tenant outputs + audit logs + manifest). Each bundle is SHA256 hashed and timestamped. For audits we can provide a 30/60/90-day historical export on request (SLA dependent).

Operational controls we will enable for the pilot: dedicated routing policy to US-only pools, KV cache TTL=5s to minimize retained context, and opt-out flag for telemetry that prevents forwarding artifacts to any model-improvement pipeline.

I'll attach the single-page ops summary and updated inventory. Dev, flag anything I missed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product (Serving) — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

(attachments: ops_summary_onepager.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_snapshot.csv)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: legal@healthworks.com, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Cole <aaron.cole@healthworks.com>, procurement@healthworks.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data use and model improvement (HealthWorks POC)

Hello all —

Confirming technical facts and schedule:

- Backup topology: HealthWorks tenant data snapshot backups are written to US-only blob storage; Country X compute nodes do not have persistent mounts for tenant backups. Replication to non-US regions is disabled for tenants with an explicit residency requirement.
- Telemetry pipelines: We will create an ingest marker for HealthWorks traffic that sets "no_improve=true" which prevents the message body, prompt, and output artifacts from entering training queues. This marker is propagated across the runtime and to downstream telemetry.
- Implementation ETA: We can have the routing policy, ingest marker, and nightly encrypted SFTP export configured and smoke-tested by 2027-07-14.

Action items for HealthWorks:
- Legal to review the attached redline and provide marked-up language by Mon 2027-07-12 if possible.
- Procurement to confirm the delivery method for escrow exports (SFTP endpoint + credentials) and DocuSign envelope for the DPA addendum.

If that's acceptable I'll stand up the US-only route in our staging cluster tomorrow and run a small pilot export to your SFTP test endpoint.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwoodinference.com

(attachments: sftp-escrow-spec.docx)
